body.statement:
For \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\) and \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}\), alternative \({\rm(ii)}\) holds: there is a rational branchwise quotient mass \(\nu\) whose image \(x\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{simp-q}}\) but not to \(\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\).  An exact nonmembership certificate is the observational polynomial implied by \(A_0\mathbin{\perp}C_0\), which vanishes on the raw image and equals \(1/4\) at \(x\).  Thus the unrestricted quotient simplex is not factorization-safe and the endpoint compiler must retain the raw product parameterization on this graph.

For general \(G\) and finite \(\mathcal J\), equality of the raw and unrestricted quotient images is decidable by the following necessary-and-sufficient factor-incidence test: for every branch \(r\) and every mass \(\nu\) on its quotient cells, there must exist a branch \(r'\) and factor weights \(\lambda\in\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r',a})\) such that
\[
\sum_C\nu(C)\overline T_{G,\mathcal J}(C)
=\sum_\kappa\left(\prod_a\lambda_a(\kappa_a)\right)T_{G,\mathcal J}(r',\kappa).
\]
This finite first-order real-algebraic condition is exact; when it holds, lexicographic minimization in its compact fibers gives a semialgebraic selector.  Moreover, the canonical catalogue may be chosen so that, with \(C=2^N+|\mathcal J|\),
\[
|\overline\Omega_{G,\mathcal J}|
\le
2^{N2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}
\min\left\{C^{N(w_G+1)/2},\,2^N3^{|\mathcal J|}\right\}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
In \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\), choose the raw branch with binary edge-latent states \(u_{AB},u_{BC}\), all private states constant, and tables
\[
A_0=u_{AB},\qquad B_0=0,\qquad C_0=u_{BC},
\]
where the table for \(C_0\) ignores its directed parent \(A_{-1}\), and set every other observed table constantly to zero.  This branch is among the deterministic systems enumerated by the raw canonical compiler.  Let \(\omega_0\) have \((u_{AB},u_{BC})=(0,0)\), let \(\omega_1\) have \((u_{AB},u_{BC})=(1,1)\), and give their two quotient cells mass \(1/2\) each.  The two cells are distinct because their observational responses differ.  The resulting rational quotient-simplex image is
\[
x=\left(\tfrac12 e_{w_0}+\tfrac12e_{w_1},\,0\right),
\tag{27}
\]
where all coordinates of \(w_i\) are zero except \(A_0=C_0=i\); the query coordinate is zero because \(C_0\) ignores \(A_{-1}\).  Hence \(x\in\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{simp-q}}\).

For every raw semi-Markovian model on \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\), the inputs of \(A_0\) are \(U_{\{A_0\}}\) and \(U_{A_0B_0}\), whereas the inputs of \(C_0\), besides its observed parent \(A_{-1}\), are \(U_{\{C_0\}}\) and \(U_{B_0C_0}\); finally, \(A_{-1}\) uses only \(U_{\{A_{-1}\}}\).  These two collections are disjoint and mutually independent.  Measurable functions of them are therefore independent, so every raw observational image satisfies \(A_0\mathbin{\perp}C_0\).  If \(P_{ij}=\Pr(A_0=i,C_0=j)\), the exact polynomial certificate is
\[
F(P)=P_{00}P_{11}-P_{01}P_{10}=0.
\tag{28}
\]
At (27), \(P_{00}=P_{11}=1/2\) and \(P_{01}=P_{10}=0\), whence \(F(P)=1/4\).  Equations (27)--(28) are a rational real-algebraic certificate that \(x\) is not in the raw image.  Thus alternative \({\rm(ii)}\) holds and, by \(\text{lem:factorized-pushforward-fidelity}\), the enlargement occurs only when factorized quotient masses are replaced by the unrestricted quotient simplex.

A non-degenerate version uses a second canonical branch in which every edge and private latent is binary, \(A_0=u_{AB}\), \(B_0=u_{\{B_0\}}\), \(C_0=u_{BC}\) (with \(C_0\) again ignoring \(A_{-1}\)), and every remaining observed vertex outputs its own private bit.  Let \(\nu^x\) put mass \(1/2\) on the two states with all private bits zero and \((u_{AB},u_{BC})=(0,0),(1,1)\), and let \(\nu^{\mathrm{unif}}\) be the quotient push-forward of independent fair weights on every latent.  The latter has uniform observational law, so the branchwise quotient mass
\[
\nu^{1/2}=\tfrac12\nu^x+\tfrac12\nu^{\mathrm{unif}}
\tag{28a}
\]
has \(P_{\nu^{1/2}}(w)\ge 2^{-(N+1)}\) for every observed cell.  Its \((A_0,C_0)\) table has diagonal entries \(3/8\) and off-diagonal entries \(1/8\), hence \(F(P_{\nu^{1/2}})=1/8\).  In the quotient-cell simplex of this branch, the set of masses \(\nu\) whose observational component \(P_\nu\) satisfies
\[
P_\nu(w)>2^{-(N+2)}\quad(w\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}),\qquad
F(P_\nu)>\tfrac1{16},\qquad
\tfrac14<\Pr_{P_\nu}(A_0=1),\Pr_{P_\nu}(C_0=1)<\tfrac34
\tag{28b}
\]
is a nonempty relative-open neighborhood of \(\nu^{1/2}\).  Every one of its laws has full observed support, \(\operatorname{Var}(A_0),\operatorname{Var}(C_0)>3/16\), and an independence-polynomial separation margin greater than \(1/16\).  Since (28) vanishes on every raw image, no point of this relative-open family has a factorized raw lift.  Thus alternative \({\rm(ii)}\) holds with a full-support, positive-variance, relative-open obstruction and, by \(\text{lem:factorized-pushforward-fidelity}\), the enlargement occurs only when factorized quotient masses are replaced by the unrestricted quotient simplex.

For the general decision statement, fix finite orderings of branches, quotient cells, factors, states, and output coordinates.  The left side of the displayed criterion is linear in \(\nu\).  Its right side is polynomial in the factor weights, with one factor in each monomial prescribed by the latent-incidence tensor.  Simplex membership is expressed by polynomial weak inequalities and linear equalities.  Thus the assertion
\[
\bigwedge_r\ \forall\nu\in\Delta(\overline\Omega_r)\ 
\bigvee_{r'}\ \exists\lambda\in\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r',a}):
A_r\nu=F_{r'}(\lambda)
\tag{29}
\]
is a finite first-order sentence over the reals.  The quotient-simplex image is \(\bigcup_r A_r\Delta(\overline\Omega_r)\), while the raw image is \(\bigcup_{r'}F_{r'}(\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r',a}))\).  The raw-to-quotient inclusion was proved in \(\text{lem:factorized-pushforward-fidelity}\); hence (29) is equivalent to the reverse inclusion and is necessary and sufficient for equality.  Real quantifier elimination from \(\text{lem:one-block-real-algebraic-elimination}\), applied successively to the finite quantifier blocks, decides (29) exactly.

When (29) holds, every fiber of candidate raw weights is nonempty and compact.  Choose the first feasible branch \(r'\), then successively minimize each coordinate of \(\lambda\) over the remaining compact fiber.  The graph of this lexicographic choice is described by the polynomial equalities together with first-order assertions that no smaller feasible coordinate exists.  Quantifier elimination makes that graph semialgebraic.  It is single-valued by lexicographic construction and gives the required selector.

It remains to prove the size bound.  Put \(C=2^N+|\mathcal J|\).  The support-reduction argument in \(\text{lem:finite-factor-support-reduction}\) permits every factor to be padded to \(C\) states without changing the attainable image.  A vertex has at most \(N-1\) observed parents and at most \(w_G\) incident exogenous factors, so its Boolean structural table has at most
\[
2^{N-1}C^{w_G}
\]
input rows and hence at most \(2^{2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}\) possible tables.  Across \(N\) vertices, a duplicate-free normalized catalogue therefore has at most
\[
2^{N2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}
\tag{30}
\]
branches.  If \(m\) is the number of exogenous factors, summing factor incidences over vertices gives
\[
N+2|E_G^{\leftrightarrow}|\le Nw_G,
\qquad
m=N+|E_G^{\leftrightarrow}|\le\frac{N(w_G+1)}2.
\tag{31}
\]
Thus a branch has at most \(C^m\le C^{N(w_G+1)/2}\) raw signatures.  Independently, \(T_{G,\mathcal J}\) has only \(2^N\) possible one-hot observational columns and \(3^{|\mathcal J|}\) possible query vectors, so a branch has at most \(2^N3^{|\mathcal J|}\) quotient cells.  Multiplying the smaller of these two per-branch bounds by (30) proves the displayed inequality.  This bound and (29) are computable, while (27)--(28) show why the untested unrestricted quotient cannot replace the raw compiler.
